# Wheel plan {#sec-dd-wheelplan}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$wheelplan
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
```

## Overview

The wheel plan is the DVLA's description of a vehicle's axles and wheels,
such as `2 AXLE RIGID BODY` or `2 WHEEL`. It separates, for example, rigid
lorries from articulated ones, and two-wheeled from three-wheeled motorcycles
(@sec-vehicle-types).

- **`wheelplan`** is the harmonised wheel plan: the DVLA value where the VES
  record describes this vehicle, and otherwise the most common value among
  vehicles of the same make, model, birth year, fuel and engine size.
- **`wheelplan_src`** says which (`dvla`, `variant` or `model_year_fuel`).
- **`wheelplan_DVLA`** is the value as supplied.

The backfill is described in the methodology,
[section 5.6](../../reports/methodology.md#other-attributes).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-wheelplan
#| tbl-cap: "Wheel plan columns."
dict_table("wheelplan")
```

## Coverage

The DVLA wheel plan is present wherever a VES record was found,
`r cov_pct(cs, "wheelplan_DVLA")` of vehicles (@sec-dd-dvla-status). Because
the wheel plan of similar vehicles is almost always known, the backfill makes
`wheelplan` nearly complete at every age: `r cov_pct(cs, "wheelplan", digits = 1)`
of vehicles (@fig-dd-wheelplan).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-wheelplan-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-wheelplan
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles with a wheel plan, as supplied by the DVLA and harmonised, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 2.6
coverage_plot(c("wheelplan_DVLA", "wheelplan"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from
1990. Each chart shows the share of vehicles with each value, with the less
common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as *Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("wheelplan"))
```
